outcomes: A failed run tells a user what failed, where it failed, and which command can reveal the full structured record
A production-profile run fails closed before execution when readiness diagnostics block it
An agent can retrieve the latest run diagnostics without spending time rerunning the jobs
A measurement consumer can collect a worktree's recorded sessions, in the order they ran, before the worktree is deleted or the store prunes them
A reader of a recorded session can tell which worktree it ran against by comparing one digest, instead of recomputing it against a tree that may have moved
A ledger or benchmark reads what each recorded run cost, over which selection, without writing its own reduction and without counting a nested run as a gate
A reader of a recorded session can tell why a task executed or reused a result from the input digest it was keyed on, without re-running the engine
A runner can identify the actual invocation's recorded plan before its tasks start, without repeating preparation in a separate planning invocation
nonGoals: Treating advisory repository hygiene findings as production blockers
Publishing secrets, configuration values, or absolute private paths in diagnostics
Making human terminal text a machine parsing contract
Making a recorded session outlive the worktree it was written in; retention bounds the store, not the worktree

requirements.text: Structured task diagnostics retain severity, code, message, and normalized file, line, and column locations through task and session results.
Human failure output prioritizes located diagnostics, bounds the live presentation, and points to structured output for the complete record.

Go and TypeScript test tasks use the same pass, fail and skip summary vocabulary; causal failure diagnostics obey the CLI report count and message limits with explicit omission accounting, while attributed transcript log events survive batch splitting as session detail.
Doctor is read-only and deterministic; production runs stop before execution on unwaived high or critical findings and fail closed when the gate is unavailable or malformed.

Doctor reports a project that has no README.md at its root as an advisory doctor.missing_readme finding, whose remediation names the purpose, commands and documentation a README states. A template project, which ships README.md.template for the project it renders, and a generated client project are exempt.
Doctor and run diagnostics never reveal configuration values, credentials, or private source contents.
The MCP diagnostic reader returns the complete diagnostics from the latest executed run in the same server session and never reruns work.
Success, failure, usage, authentication, API, and interruption outcomes map to stable documented exit codes and machine-result statuses.

Machine JSONL suppresses debug task detail in normal mode, admits it in verbose mode under fixed deterministic budgets, protects failure capacity, reports exact elision, applies terminal-safe redaction, and retains a complete sanitized session artifact without changing task or run semantics.

The opening scheduler:parallel event carries optional event.sessionId after its v2 plan is written and before tasks start. Verification and publish-containing runs use the same path and prepare once. Live and retained streams agree; sessionless schedulers omit the ID. Readers bind their invocation's event to .putnami/sessions/<sessionId>/plan.json as advisory, untrusted input. Envelopes, budgets, nested attribution and verdicts are unchanged; missing or elided events provide no early evidence.

Export emits every recorded session still present, oldest first by recorded start time, deduplicated by session id, forwarding the recorded document verbatim so a member a newer producer added survives. --since filters on the recorded start time and is inclusive at the boundary. Retention is configurable per workspace and its default is unchanged.

`putnami tree fingerprint` prints one digest covering HEAD, the bytes at every tracked path that differs from it (recursing through submodules), and the content of every untracked non-ignored file, from anywhere inside the worktree and without a workspace. A recorded session carries that same digest, captured before its first task ran, together with the dirty verdict and the head it was taken against. A producer that cannot determine the tree records no tree block rather than claiming a clean one.

`putnami tree verify` checks an execute run's local evidence against the worktree it runs in and prints one JSON verdict on stdout, whatever the output mode, without a workspace. A failure, a bare call included, prints {"verdict":"not-verified","reason":...} on one line, exits 1 and writes nothing on stderr. Evidence is read as fatal UTF-8, an object that repeats a member is refused, and every path resolves against the Git top level.

Summary reduces each recorded session to one row: id, start, commands, selection, tasks total/executed/reused, run.cpu.actualMs, wall and outcome, in export's order and with its deduplication. A run a task spawned names its parent and is marked nested, never counted as a run of its own: --command keeps top-level sessions whose command set is exactly the named list, in any order, and never a nested run whatever it ran. Structured output carries the rows as an array at every count.

Every task record that reached a verdict carries inputDigest: the cache key it was keyed on, spelled sha256: and 64 lowercase hex, so it moves exactly when the key does. A skipped record and a task with no cache identity carry none. Summary --by-digest groups the selected sessions' records by digest in first-recorded order, with records, executed, reused and failed counts and each occurrence's session and reuse; records without a digest are counted apart.
